name: Employment Permit and Residence Permit (Employed)

requirements.blocker_text: The prospective employer must request an employment permit from the Department of Labor Affairs before the applicant can apply for a residence permit -- an employee cannot self-initiate this route.
First-time applicants generally cannot be present on the island while the residence permit application is being processed.

evidence_required.document: Employment permit issued by the Department of Labor Affairs

outcome.duration_length: temporary, extendable (Model 3 extension applications may be filed up to 4 months before expiry)

sources.title: Ministry of Justice, Government of Sint Maarten -- Immigration and Border Protection Services: employer-obtained employment permit precondition, 6-week-to-3-month residence permit processing, applicant must be outside the island during first-time processing, 4-month pre-expiry extension window, 5-year path to permanent residency
Government of Sint Maarten -- Department of Labor Affairs: Section Permits processes employment permit requests (contact details only; no published fee or detailed criteria)

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Sint Maarten's initial build. No fee schedule or numeric duration cap was found on either official page reviewed -- flagged as a gap; the Department of Labor Affairs page in particular gave almost no substantive detail beyond confirming the office exists and handles permit processing. work_rights is 'restricted' (tied to the specific employer/position underlying the employment permit). leads_to_pr/pr_after_months (60 months) reflects the immigration overview page's own explicit statement that 'after 5 years of consecutive legal residency, applicants may pursue permanent residency' -- see sx_permanent_residence.json.
